statement: Seven residue classes: config env whose holder died; tests encoding the removed contract; names outliving referents; generated artifacts; cross-package hardcoded paths; documentation describing a deleted harness; and local machine state outside the repository.
mechanism: each class needs a different instrument; none is closed by a single grep

statement: The deleted MCP blocks carried five _NOTE_* documentation keys alongside the values, two of which documented live invariants (the DB override chain and the fail-closed trust rule). Re-homing the values to the launcher did not re-home the documentation, which now exists only in git.
mechanism: a residue sweep for retired tokens cannot see content that is absent rather than stale

statement: The alias defect visible in code and the self-contradictory _NOTE_DB prose are one event seen twice: a mechanized rename replaced both members of an alias pair, once in an operand chain and once in a documenting string, and the block deletion then removed the last record of the intent.
mechanism: a find-and-replace that rewrites every occurrence cannot preserve an alias pair, in code or in prose

statement: Tests encoding a removed contract are red or unresolvable, not silently green, so tooling finds them as soon as a full suite samples them. The packet's rule that a defect found during a sweep is raised rather than rewritten is what preserved the count.
mechanism: detection is a sampling property, not a discovery problem

statement: A name is residue only when its referent is dead. mcpServerDir in the CLI shim is a lying identifier whose value is now runtime/; the mcp trigger aliases are correct names because users do type mcp. Identical tokens, opposite dispositions, and the instrument sees only the token.
mechanism: disposition depends on a fact about the world, not about the string

statement: Generated artifacts are stale by construction, their regeneration is all-or-nothing, and their consumers may depend on the existing drift; the trigger index additionally constrains what the documentation may be renamed to, so residue is also a fence.
mechanism: derived, non-separable, and occasionally load-bearing drift

statement: 603 mcp-server/ references survive outside the advisor skill directory (sk-code 67, system-spec-kit 51, sk-doc 36, sk-design 23, system-deep-loop 19, cli-external-orchestration 12, skills/.state 11, others fewer), because the sweep's scope was the skill directory. A tranche-scoped grep returns clean while the path still resolves from outside the tranche.
evidence: measured: grep -rn 'mcp-server/' over .opencode/**/*.md excluding node_modules, dist and advisor changelog
mechanism: scope boundary, not search technique, is what leaves this class behind

statement: The sharpest documentation residue is not stale prose but a live diagnostic describing a present that no longer exists: mcp-doctor.sh screens servers=(system_skill_advisor code_mode) unconditionally, warns Not wired on every run, and prints the deleted mcp-server/node_modules at lines 300,303,399 while testing the correct runtime path.
mechanism: a present-tense false claim that also acts on the world; a token-organised sweep puts it in the same bucket as honest history

statement: Rewrite of the launcher status file to a temporary database path, the generation counter under .opencode/skills/.state/advisor/ that honours no override, and a stray benchmark daemon are residue that no grep of the tree and no git operation can reach.
mechanism: residue in the environment rather than the corpus, discoverable only by inspecting a run's side effects

approach: Treating name residue as one class closed by a token sweep
reason: mcpServerDir and the mcp trigger aliases share the token and require opposite dispositions

approach: Handling generated artifacts with a blanket regenerate-after-rename step
reason: One generator run rewrote 18,966 unrelated lines and shifted advisor fusion scores; the manifest generator fails on an unrelated resolution defect

label: Which residue classes does tooling find unaided, and which require reading?
